parsed.rationale: All three members — `Announcement.CodingKeys`, `Breakpoint.CodingKeys`, and `Talkset.CodingKeys` — are flagged as `exact-duplicates` with `shared_field_count: 4` and `jaccard: null` (indicating identical shape), all residing in the same `Playlist` package. Because they are `type-alias-union` kinds that are structurally identical, maintaining three separate declarations creates a silent divergence risk: a future field added to one `CodingKeys` must be manually mirrored in the other two. Consolidating to a single shared definition in `Shared/Playlist/Sources/Playlist/` eliminates that risk with no loss of expressiveness.

specifics.proposed_action: Define a single shared `CodingKeys` enum (or typealias) in the `Playlist` package — for example as a top-level `PlaylistEntryCodingKeys` enum, or as a protocol `PlaylistEntryCodable` with an associated `CodingKeys` — and have `Announcement`, `Breakpoint`, and `Talkset` each reuse it. Remove the three identical nested `CodingKeys` type-alias-union declarations at `_Plant_Announcement.swift:34`, `PlaylistEntry.swift:72`, and `PlaylistEntry.swift:111`.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The three members are `type-alias-union` kinds (not plain enums, structs, or functions), so neither `generic-parameterization`, `subclass-lift`, nor `default-implementation` applies directly. `extract-to-common` is the closest named category, but the records are already in the same package (`Playlist`) and the same or adjacent files, so the extraction is intra-package consolidation rather than a cross-package move. The most idiomatic Swift fix is to hoist the shared `CodingKeys` definition to a single declaration site within `Playlist` and have all three types reference it, which is best described as an intra-package deduplication that doesn't map cleanly to any single named category.
